quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Drive close to the parked vehicles to give moving traffic more room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your vehicle and parked cars. A person may step out without looking. A parked driver may start moving their vehicle without seeing you.

questions.question: At a flashing red light, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
Slow down and keep going with caution.
Stop and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must come to a full stop and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop Sign Ahead.
Side Road.
Railroad Warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop Sign Ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Use only your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, put your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly out the rear window. Mirrors don't show everything behind your vehicle. Back up slowly.

questions.question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?

options.text: Prescription drugs are safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
Only illegal drugs can affect your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can make it harder to drive safely. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and anxiety. It is illegal to drive while impaired by any drug—whether illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.
At all times.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes (with or without a red tip).

questions.question: If you park in an unusual spot, you should:

options.text: Park with your reverse lights on.
Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
Park five feet away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
questions.explanation: You must make sure your parked vehicle is not a hazard. Park where other drivers can see your car from any direction.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and go slowly.
Look left and right to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that appear to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left and right to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: At any place where people may cross or traffic lines meet, look to both sides of your vehicle to make sure nothing is coming.

questions.question: A red painted curb means:

options.text: Loading zone.
The area is for picking up or dropping off passengers.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red curb.

questions.question: A car ahead has high beams on and is blinding you at night. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Don't look directly at the headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other vehicle from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution. You do not need to stop completely.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Come to a complete stop at the intersection.
Maintain your normal speed.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means be alert and careful. Slow down before you proceed through the intersection.

questions.question: Where is it illegal to park?

options.text: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
Within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: You cannot park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. You also cannot park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, how can other drivers see you better?

options.text: Turn up the instrument panel lights.
Turn on your parking lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when visibility is low or when other drivers may have trouble seeing you. Turn on your low beam headlights if you need to use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: What does a red and white yield sign mean?

options.text: Stop and check for traffic from both directions before proceeding.
Give the right-of-way to traffic on the road you want to enter or cross.
Keep a steady speed and check for traffic from all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to traffic on the road you want to enter or cross.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means slow down and be ready to stop if needed. Let other vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians pass before you proceed. You do not have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What blood alcohol level makes a DUI conviction legal?

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
50 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: A blood alcohol level of 0.08 percent is always illegal for driving. Drivers under age 21 face penalties at 0.02 percent or higher. You can be convicted of DUI even if your blood alcohol is below 0.08 percent.

questions.question: If you cannot find a gap in traffic to enter the freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and force other drivers to make room.
Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a safe gap in traffic. Do not stop at the ramp's end because you will not have enough space to speed up and match the traffic flow.

questions.question: Where should you place your hands on the steering wheel?

options.text: At 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock positions.
At 11 o'clock and 6 o'clock positions.
At 7 o'clock and 5 o'clock positions.

questions.correctAnswerText: At 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock positions.
questions.explanation: Place your left hand at 9 o'clock and your right hand at 3 o'clock on the steering wheel, like a clock face.

questions.question: How can you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror regularly to stay aware of traffic behind you.

questions.question: When is a U-turn not permitted?

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near a curve or hill.
On a straight road with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near a curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians and could cause a crash.

questions.question: Which of the following blocks traffic flow?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes causes traffic jams and should be avoided.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on the upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns about a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to control your speed to protect your brakes.

questions.question: You must show proof of insurance to police:

options.text: Only if you are in a crash.
If you are in a crash or stopped for a ticket.
Only if you are stopped and given a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a crash or stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance when driving. You must show your insurance proof and license to a police officer when asked after a traffic stop or crash.

questions.question: Interstate driving requires drivers to:

options.text: Be able to safely drive at higher speeds.
Stay alert at all times.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving requires you to stay alert and be able to drive at high speeds.

questions.question: The amount of alcohol in your blood is called:

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC means a person is more impaired.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. You should:

options.text: Slow down when driving.
Look constantly in all directions.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look constantly in all directions.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can hide in your blind spot or be missed because they are small. Car drivers must always look for motorcycles, mopeds, and scooters.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the right edge of the road and slow down.
Move to the right edge of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using its siren and lights. Move to the right edge and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through first, then stop.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, you should:

options.text: Use low beam headlights.
Use high beam headlights until you are 10 feet from the vehicle ahead.
Use high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use high beams only in rural areas when no other cars are nearby. Switch to low beams when following closely behind another vehicle.

questions.question: If the road ahead is flooded, you should:

options.text: Hit the brakes hard.
Do not drive through it. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through it. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive on a flooded road. Even shallow water can hide dangers. If you find a flooded area, turn around and take a different route.

questions.question: Excessive speed:

options.text: Saves time so you arrive faster.
Helps you get around obstacles.
Increases the risk of serious injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of serious injury and death.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and leads to dangerous driving choices.
